target.title: fix(acp): order new session response before updates
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #109961.

ACP `session/new` currently emits initial `session/update` notifications before returning the JSON-RPC result that introduces the new `sessionId`. Clients that require the result before accepting updates can discard the early notification and leave the new session unable to proceed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`AcpGatewayAgent.newSession()` must gather and emit the initial snapshot through the ACP connection before its handler can return. The SDK serializes the request result only after that handler resolves, so changing awaits inside the translator cannot guarantee wire order.

This change enforces the invariant at the stdio protocol boundary. It buffers only `session/update` notifications for session IDs the client has not learned yet. When the matching new-session result arrives, the result is forwarded first and buffered updates follow in their original order. Session IDs supplied by clients, such as `session/load`, are marked as already known and continue streaming without delay.

## User Impact

ACP clients now always receive the `session/new` result before initial metadata, usage, or command updates that reference the returned `sessionId`. Existing-session flows retain their current streaming behavior.

## Evidence

- `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/acp/session-new-ordering.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (4 tests passed)
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/acp/session-new-ordering.ts src/acp/session-new-ordering.test.ts src/acp/server.ts`
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/acp/session-new-ordering.ts src/acp/session-new-ordering.test.ts src/acp/server.ts`
- `src/acp/server.startup.test.ts`: 17/18 tests passed locally; the remaining environment-only test was blocked because local Node 25.2.1 links SQLite 3.51.2, which OpenClaw correctly rejects under its WAL safety gate.

AI-assisted with Codex. The implementation and tests were reviewed and run locally by the contributor.
